name: mnemonic_scavenger_map
label: The Silence's Consumption Map
godotFeature: ShaderMaterial on Control nodes with ViewportTexture and procedural UV modification
poeticVision: Feel the horrifying urgency as the very map you rely on visibly degrades and gets 'eaten' by tendrils of the Silence, live, during a chase. You lose not just position, but the *meaning* of landmarks, the *directionality* of your escape. It's a race against not just physical hunters, but against the map itself dissolving into incomprehensible static, blurring the line between navigating a memory and succumbing to its loss.

parameters.name: shader_path
parameters.description: Path to the GLSL shader file (`.gdshader`) that defines the map degradation effect.

parameters.name: degradation_amount
parameters.description: The current level of map degradation, ranging from 0.0 (no degradation) to 1.0 (fully consumed). This value should be updated by game logic.

parameters.name: degradation_origin
parameters.description: The UV coordinate (0,0 to 1,1) on the map where the degradation effect originates. This can be set to follow the player or a specific threat.

parameters.name: degradation_speed
parameters.description: An optional rate at which `degradation_amount` increases per second. This is for demonstration or simple auto-degradation; typically, `degradation_amount` is controlled externally.

verdict: A brilliant fusion of UI and narrative, this invention transforms a mere map into a living, dying testament to Lyra's fading self, making every lost landmark a shard of her soul.
impact: This mechanic will fundamentally alter how players perceive and interact with the game world. Navigation, typically a static utility, becomes a dynamic, high-stakes challenge. It will amplify the feeling of existential dread and urgency, forcing players to internalize memory fragments and spatial awareness as their external aids literally dissolve. The map's degradation will serve as a constant, visceral reminder of Lyra's fading identity, making every chase not just a fight for physical survival but a desperate struggle against mental erasure.
